scope: Issue #3 adaptive/hard-budget policy slice and Zen free-tier tool visibility compatibility
testedRuntimeSource: Runtime and controlled E2E harness were tested from commit 81a352675f524e2c0a4dfecea6b7aa7b956b402e on OpenCode 2.0.11. The runtime deny raises @opencode/schema Tool.Error; the real Promise adapter serializes the rejection as an OpenCode tool error with type=unknown. The E2E records that representation rather than claiming typed Tool.Error propagation.

rootCause.historicalProviderThrottle: Earlier gateway runs recorded real 429s and resource-budget:rate-high. Those runs remain valid evidence of provider throttling; the governor correctly stopped additional spend.
rootCause.authenticatedBlocker: A later authenticated run no longer showed the old rate-high symptom. It instead exposed provider.auth 403 stating that the OpenCode free tier could only be used within OpenCode; internal critic/orchestrator tool restrictions were removing tools from the provider-facing request.
rootCause.correction: Critic and orchestrator sessions now advertise the Zen-compatible toolset. Their local authority remains a fail-closed execute.before boundary using control-plane session metadata; only read/glob/grep execute for these roles. Worker keeps its own permission boundary.
rootCause.upstreamContext: OpenCode issues anomalyco/opencode#50627 and #49723 were cited as matching upstream reports. They are upstream context, not OPJEV runtime evidence.
rootCause.currentGatewayObservation: The authenticated gateway run below passed all 55 assertions; no provider.auth 403, 429/529, or resource-budget denial was observed in the run summary.

The six policy cases are restored/reworked in src/readonly-policy.test.mjs, and all nine tool-authority tests now reside in src/tool-authority.test.mjs and run under npm test.

multiroundReal.runtime: OpenCode 2.0.11; live Jev SystemOne + controlled provider fault/tool-call boundary
multiroundReal.scenario7: Provider tool visibility remains real and compatible; scenario 18 independently proves local execute.before authority at runtime.

securityEvidence.localBoundary: Runtime E2E scenario 18 uses real critic/orchestrator sessions, real OPJEV server plugin, @opencode/plugin 2.0.7 Promise adapter, real OpenCode tool registry, and controlled provider execute tool calls. OPJEV raises @opencode/schema Tool.Error. The Promise adapter wraps callback promises in Effect.promise; OpenCode records the rejection as tool error type=unknown, with executed=false. Both sessions complete, the host stays healthy, and no canary, worker, Jev call, retry storm, or dispatch occurs. This is runtime evidence of enforced denial; it does not claim typed Tool.Error propagation through the adapter.
securityEvidence.canaryTests: src/tool-authority.test.mjs and adapter hook tests call the registered boundary before a canary executor and assert zero invocation for shell, edit/write, subagent/task, execute/code, question, web and unknown tools; orchestrator has the same rule. Worker isolation and ambiguous/missing control-plane metadata fail-closed cases are covered.
securityEvidence.gatewayScope: The gateway E2E proves the plugin was loaded and the real orchestration/follow-up/TUI path completed. It did not ask a live model to attempt a forbidden critic/orchestrator tool call; the explicit zero-executor canaries are deterministic local hook tests.
securityEvidence.providerCompatibility: Separately proven through the real gateway; provider visibility does not grant local execution authority.

limitations: Provider quota reset times and remaining quota are unavailable; Issue #3 uses a local 15-minute heuristic window, not a provider reset claim.
The serialized throttle reservation is process-local and does not provide cross-process atomicity.
The evaluator tool boundary depends on OpenCode 2.0.11 execute.before behavior and control-plane session metadata; unknown internal state fails closed.
No fan-out telemetry is fabricated. Issue #3 remains open for maintainer evaluation against all remaining criteria.

OpenCode 2.0.7 Promise adapter converts the rejected Tool.Error to an OpenCode tool error with type=unknown. The runtime E2E proves this is bounded and non-fatal in OpenCode 2.0.11 (executor skipped, host healthy); typed Tool.Error propagation is not preserved by this adapter path.

Latest gateway reruns on tested HEAD observed real provider 429 throttles and Resource Governor denial (51/55); the previously accepted 55/55 artifact is retained under lastKnownGreenBeforeThisChange. No provider.auth 403 appeared.
